name: YOLO-NAS
paper_title: YOLO-NAS: A Next-Generation, Object Detection Foundational Model generated by Deci's Neural Architecture Search Technology
license_interpretation: Two licenses apply here and they are not the same. The SuperGradients source this port follows is Apache-2.0 and LibreYOLO's own implementation is MIT, so nothing restricts the architecture or the training code. Deci's published checkpoints are a different matter: the YOLO-NAS license grants a revocable, non-transferable right to use them and nothing more. It forbids redistribution and sublicensing, forbids offering them as a managed or remote service, restricts modification and reverse engineering, and rules out commercial use, including any model running in a production environment, unless you hold a separate agreement with Deci. LibreYOLO therefore does not mirror them, and prints those terms once before the download starts. Weights trained from a randomly initialized model on your own data derive from no Deci checkpoint.

bibtex_verified: 2026-08-08, copied verbatim from the Citing section of the upstream README on branch master. YOLO-NAS was released without a paper, so this SuperGradients entry is the citation its authors ask for. Cross-checked against the Zenodo record the entry's DOI resolves to, 10.5281/zenodo.7789328: the record is the software release Deci-AI/super-gradients 3.0.8, deposited 2023-03-31, and every author named in the entry appears in its creator list in the same relative order, alongside further contributors the entry omits. The year field reads 2021, the year the repository started rather than the year of the deposit, and is left as the authors wrote it. Do not hand-edit; a wrong citation misattributes someone's work.
